items.title: 70980_Quinn Wilson oral history interview
items.q: I went with Erskine Tate. And -- no, Walter Barnes' bass player, we switched jobs.

ctx.x: Well, I was still -- I was with Earl Hines, then. This was back in the thirties. They got trapped in a dance. I worked with him for a little while, and then Erskine Tate heard about me. And he wanted me to come with his band. So that's the reason I had to get on the bass fiddle. Because this was playing for silent pictures in the moving picture theater pit.
Now, with all the other bands you'd been playing tuba. And they had arrangements? It wasn't, you know, a "fake" band?
